summary: Typosquat CKEditor build: preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: @onereach/ckeditor5-build-classic 30.0.2 impersonates @ckeditor/ckeditor5-build-classic — copying the description, author ("CKSource"), homepage (ckeditor.com), and README of the legitimate package, but publishing under an unrelated scope and adding a preinstall lifecycle hook the genuine package does not have. The preinstall script (setup.mjs) is itself obfuscated in obfuscator.io style (_0x-prefixed identifiers, property-map indirection hiding strings such as `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`, `bun`, `unzip`, `powershell`, `Expand-Archive`). On install it downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (bun-v1.3.13), unzips it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a package-local file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB `@bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle using a string-array rotator decoder (~1000-entry literal table) and hex-mangled identifiers. Fetching a second JavaScript runtime solely to execute a shipped obfuscated bundle at install time evades Node-based sandboxes and inspection; a rich-text-editor build has no need for either an alternate runtime or an obfuscated auxiliary script. This is the alternate-runtime dropper shape combined with brand-impersonation metadata.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
